questions.question: How did the Magna Carta influence modern democracies? / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Magna Carta limited absolute monarchy -established the principle that rulers are subject
  • to law - inspiring modern democratic ideals such as due process, equality before law, and
  • protection of individual rights.
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: How did Gandhi’s philosophy influence global human rights movements? / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Gandhi’s philosophy inspired global human rights movements - through non -violence,
  • truth, and civil disobedience -his ideas influenced leaders like Martin Luther King Jr. and
  • Nelson Mandela in fighting injustice peacefully - non-violence - civil disobedience - human
  • dignity.

questions.question: How does NHRC contribute to strengthening democracy in India? / [CO2]

  • rights violations, recommending reforms- spreading awareness on constitutional rights and
  • justice for marginalized communities.

  • improving administrative efficiency - transparency - accountability - anti-corruption.

questions.question: Why is Ram Mohan Roy considered a pioneer of human rights in India? / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Ram Mohan Roy pioneered human rights by challenging social evils like sati - promoting
  • freedom of speech, women’s rights, education, and rationalism - laying the foundation for
  • modern reform movements in India.

questions.question: Why is individual liberty central to liberal human rights? / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Individual liberty is central to liberal human rights - because it guarantees freedom of
  • thought, expression and personal choice- limits state interference while protecting individual
  • dignity and democratic participation.- freedom - autonomy – equality.

questions.question: Explain the scope of judicial review in India? / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• Judicial review allows courts to examine the constitutionality of laws and executive
  • actions, ensuring they align with the Constitution -protecting citizens’ rights from arbitrary
  • or unlawful government actions.

questions.question: How does custodial killing undermine the rule of law? / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• Custodial killing undermines the rule of law by violating the right to life and due process-
  • weakens public trust- encourages abuse of power and denies justice through unlawful actions
  • - human rights violation - abuse of authority - loss of public trust.

questions.question: Analyze the obstacles that prevent persons with disabilities from accessing education and employment opportunities in India. / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• Persons with disabilities face barriers such as inaccessible infrastructure, social stigma -
  • lack of inclusive education, and inadequate job opportunities - preventing their full
  • participation in education and employment sectors.
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Evaluate the effectiveness of HRLN’s litigation and advocacy in influencing policy reforms on human rights issues. / [CO4]

  • litigation (PIL), legal aid, and integrated advocacy-HRLN’s strategic litigation and advocacy

  • justice for vulnerable groups- pressing governments to implement rights-based policies.

questions.question: How does bulldozer justice conflict with the rule of law? / [CO2] [5x6 = 30]
questions.solution_html:
• Bulldozer justice violates the rule of law by bypassing legal procedures, denying fair
  • hearings, and promoting arbitrary state action, undermining judicial authority, due process,
  • and citizens’ constitutional rights.

  • groups through equal access to learning - equal opportunity - social inclusion –
  • empowerment.

questions.question: Analyse the impact of the UDHR on international human rights movements. / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• UDHR profoundly influenced international human rights movements by establishing a
  • universal framework for dignity, equality, and freedom -inspired global treaties, national
  • constitutions, and activism- leading to institutions and norms that protect individuals from
  • state abuse and promote justice worldwide.
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: How does the UDHR promote global cooperation on human rights issues? / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR) provides a common global standard for
  • protecting human rights-encourages nations to adopt human rights laws -cooperate through
  • international organizations and promote equality, justice, and peace - guides treaties and
  • national constitutions while strengthening international accountability for human rights
  • violations- universal standards - international cooperation - human dignity

questions.question: Compare the Right to Equality and the Right to Freedom. Examine its relevance in creating a democratic polity in India. / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• Right to Equality ensures equal treatment before law, while the Right to Freedom
  • guarantees expression, movement, and association-together, they empower citizens, prevent
  • discrimination, and enable participation in governance - forming the moral and legal
  • foundation of India’s democratic and inclusive political system.
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Explain the concept of judicial review and its constitutional basis in India. Discuss its significance in maintaining the rule of law and protecting fundamental rights.” / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• Judicial review is the power of the judiciary to examine the constitutional validity of laws
  • and executive actions - basis lies in Articles 13, 32, 131 –136, 226, and 227 of the Indian
  • Constitution-upholds the Constitution- protects Fundamental Rights and ensures the rule of
  • law by preventing arbitrary use of power - - constitutional supremacy - protection of rights -
  • checks and balances.
questions.source_exam: III Semester MGU-UGP-(Hons) 2024 Admission Regular(Special Examination) Examination July 2026

questions.question: Examine the significance of the Vishaka Guidelines and the POSH Act in promoting a safe and harassment-free workplace for women in India / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• Vishaka Guidelines (1997) and the POSH Act (2013) defined and criminalized workplace
  • sexual harassment - making employers responsible for prevention and redressal -they
  • institutionalized gender -sensitive mechanisms - empowering women to work safely and
  • promoting equality, dignity, and justice within India’s professional and social spaces.
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: "Despite constitutional safeguards, vulnerable groups in India still face numerous challenges.” Discuss this statement with reference to women, children, and transgender persons. / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• Despite constitutional safeguards, vulnerable groups continue to face discrimination and
  • inequality-women experience gender violence and unequal opportunities- children face child
  • labour and abuse - transgender persons encounter social exclusion and employment
  • discrimination-effective implementation of laws - awareness and inclusive policies are
  • essential for ensuring equality and dignity - social discrimination - legal protection - inclusive
  • development.
questions.source_exam: III Semester MGU-UGP-(Hons) 2024 Admission Regular(Special Examination) Examination July 2026

questions.question: Examine Right to Privacy as an essential component of human rights and evaluate its significance in safeguarding individual freedom / [CO4] [15x2 = 30]
questions.solution_html:
• Right to Privacy- upheld in the Puttaswamy judgment (2017)- vital to human dignity and
  • autonomy-safeguards individuals from state surveillance, data misuse, and intrusion,
  • ensuring personal liberty, freedom of choice, democratic accountability—core components of
  • modern human rights protection.
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Critically analyze how the Aadhaar project has raised constitutional concerns relating to the right to privacy under Article 21. / [CO4] [15x2 = 30]
questions.solution_html:
• Aadhaar project raised constitutional concerns - regarding the Right to Privacy under
  • Article 21 due to the collection and storage of biometric and personal data - Supreme Court
  • recognized privacy as a Fundamental Right while permitting Aadhaar with safeguards
  • against misuse, ensuring proportionality, data protection, and limited mandatory use - right
  • to privacy - data protection - constitutional safeguards.
